payload.title: When a run has taught me that a Goal is wrong or outgrown, I say so once in my own words. After that nothing of it is owed or waits for me, and a later Goal can point at my end.
payload.body:
Issue #177. Today a Goal I no longer want stays in progress forever: its readings wait for me and its items stay owed, and a later Goal cannot point at the fact that I gave it up. This Goal adds the owner's end: one terminal act, in the owner's words, that replay reads as the Goal state "ended".

The base is main at 8cd0c6e. The change is a new ADR that names the end as an exception to owner rules 3 and 5 of docs/principles.md §7, and to §2's "a later event can move the status again". The glossary gains "end" and "ended". The same commits fix every sentence in skills/, docs/, README.md and AGENTS.md that the change makes false, such as the cite and Hand-off sentences of skills/hyp-owner-grill, the `hyp prompt` exit sentence of skills/hyp-owner-answer, principles §7, ADR 0020's cite table, and the replay spec's answer and cite rules and its sentence that `hyp prompt` reads no answer.

Each Experiment whose commit changes skill prose reviews that prose by ak-skill-creator's update, audit and optimize flow, beside `go test`.

A Goal added by a runner actor before this change can be ended only under that runner's name.

The first use of the end, on record:G-SZCBXZ, record:G-BPWZ24 and record:G-4N85GM, waits until the new binary is installed: an older hyp rejects the field.

Kinds of case these lines do not place are left unplaced. Where a builder's test and a reviewer's test disagree on one, it is a reading at the stop.

Out of scope: a tool that lands a record (#203); the grill's Start entry for an ended Goal and its base rule (#205); a run rule against sub-questions under a held candidate; readings on withdrawn questions of live Goals; `hyp status --all`, which is not on main. When `--all` lands, it prints nothing of an ended Goal under OWED or AWAITING OWNER.

Lines that hold on the base: line 7's last sentence. The replay half of line 2 is green on base only because the base rejects any unknown field, so its tests assert the rule's own reason.

May change: hyp's code, tests and docs (internal/, cmd/, docs/, skills/, README.md, AGENTS.md) by commits on branch feat/goal-end cut from main, pushed as one PR the run never merges
May change: investigations/goal-end, written with the installed hyp on a branch cut from main that holds only .tree/ changes, in its own worktree, pushed as a record PR the owner merges at every stop
Read only: every other store under investigations/, and recipes/
Never: replace the installed hyp binary
Never: write an event under the owner's actor
Never: run hyp answer --end
Never: merge a PR, or edit or remove a recorded event

lines.text: [P] When the actor that added Goal G runs `hyp answer --end G=TEXT`, on G in progress or complete, it exits 0. After it, `hyp status` and `hyp show G` read G as ended in place of in_progress or complete, and print TEXT.
[N] An end of G by any other actor is refused at write with exit 1, naming the rule, and a log that holds one is rejected on replay.

[N] A second end of G, or one answer that ends G and also moves a key of G, is refused at write with exit 1. In a merged log, the first end of G by id order applies, and the later end or the mixed answer is rejected on replay.

[P] An ended Goal shows nothing that waits: none of its items under OWED or AWAITING OWNER; no question of it shown as waiting on an open reading or a referred limit; its GOALS row reads ended. `hyp show` still prints its lines, readings, limits and Results.

[N] A write whose node leads to an ended Goal is refused at write with exit 1, naming the end. This covers adds under it, Results, retracts, selects, defers, withdraws, resumes, subjects, edges from its nodes, checkpoints, and answer items on its keys. Replay applies such an event when it is merged after the end, and `hyp check` warns. `hyp add goal` and cites from other Goals stay admitted.
[N] `hyp prompt` for an ended Goal exits 1, names the end, and prints nothing on stdout.

[P] Ending a Goal settles every key of it, so a later line may cite the ended Goal's id, which reads "ended", and any of its keys; a key not settled before the end reads "ended". `hyp show` of the line prints the end's words beside the cite. A line written before the end prints that its Goal has since ended. The id of a Goal not ended is refused as a cite with exit 1.

[P] `skills/hyp-owner-answer/SKILL.md` names `hyp answer --end` as an owner move, with the four ways out for "I don't know": leave it open, a test, "show me" as a sub-question (only on the owner's words), or end the Goal. It says that only an answer session types `--end`, and that a turn that ends a Goal writes no runner checkpoint on it.

[P] The read-back in `skills/hyp-owner-grill/SKILL.md` checks the dry-written text only against what the grill settled and against the code. It has no rule that a rerun must raise no unplaced kind of case, and it sends no kind the grill never settled to the owner as a placement: such a kind is left unplaced, for the run to raise as a reading.

why: grill of #177, cut by source on the owner's decision; no fresh-reader read-back, which departs from the grill skill (see #205)

answers.text: They should depend on the state. If there is no state to keep it, it's a gap.
'its Goal' means the line's own Goal

ends.text: I will not finish #177 in this state, so I stop it here. #208 was reviewed and merged as it is, without the hyp tree. What is left is R-471081#r1: what hyp prints should depend on the state; if there is no state to keep it, it's a gap.

Events: #162 (raised text prints three ways); R-471081#r1 (turn words do not read a state); the /goal stop rule quotes a printed sentence of hyp status (internal/cli/prompt.go); replay and render decide 'separates' by different rules (internal/replay/separated.go, internal/render/status.go).

lines.text: [P] The communication channel, which is used for `hyp` to communicate with agent, is one block of code, defined with Go as code that has a boundary, such as one Go module, one object or one state machine.
[N] Two commands can give different answers about the same fact.
[N] hyp tells the owner and the agent something its state doesn't hold.

why: Owner, 2026-11-15: the #183 Goal, in the owner's words
